newsitem.title: EGYPT: France's de Charette in Cairo for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: France's de Charette in Cairo for peace talks.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette arrived in Cairo on Monday for talks with Egyptian officials on increasing France's involvement in the Middle East peace process.

"I am here to meet my friend (Egyptian Foreign Minister) Amr Moussa to discuss the latest developments in the region and the European and French role in the peace process," de Charette told reporters at Cairo airport.
"The European role is very important and beneficial for any quick solution to the Middle East peace process," he added.
De Charette will also hold talks with Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel Meguid and may meet Mubarak during his two-day visit, officials said.
The 15-nation European Union is keen to boost its role in the region from mere paymaster to a political partner which may even join the United States in co-sponsoring the peace talks.
Arabs have traditionally seen the U.S. role as tilted towards Israel and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has repeatedly called on the EU to step in and balance things out.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi held talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Monday on how to boost Europe's role in the region and French President Jacques Chirac will also visit Cairo on Friday for similar talks.

Chirac is currently visiting Israel as part of a peace-promoting tour of the region but de Charette boycotted the visit after the Jewish state refused to let him visit Orient House, the headquarters of the Palestinian Authority in disputed Arab East Jerusalem.
Israel gave Chirac a cool welcome on Monday and the right-leaning Jerusalem Post daily slammed France as a "biased would-be broker."
